## How to use this

The code from Lecture 20, run, with the numbers it produces, and the challenge
solved.

. . .

Your last decimal place may differ from mine. Anything beyond that is worth
asking about.

::: {.notes}
Posted after class so nobody is left wondering whether their answer was right.
:::

## Setting up {.smaller}

```{r}
base <- "https://github.com/bmaitner/biometry_course/raw/refs/heads/main/data/class_examples/"
occ <- read.csv(paste0(base, "bobwhite_occupancy.csv"))
counts <- read.csv(paste0(base, "bobwhite_counts.csv"))
reef <- read.csv(paste0(base, "reef_surveys.csv"))
```

With the course package installed, `bobwhite_occupancy`, `bobwhite_counts` and
`reef_surveys` give the same tables.

## Fix 1: centering {.smaller}

```{r}
year_nll <- function(p, x){
  prob <- plogis(p[1] + p[2] * x)
  -sum(dbinom(occ$n_occupied, size = occ$n_routes, prob = prob, log = TRUE))
}

fit_raw <- optim(c(0, 0), year_nll, x = occ$year, method = "BFGS")
c(nll = fit_raw$value, convergence = fit_raw$convergence)

occ$c_year <- occ$year - mean(occ$year)
fit_cen <- optim(c(0, 0), year_nll, x = occ$c_year, method = "BFGS")
c(fit_cen$par, nll = fit_cen$value, convergence = fit_cen$convergence)
```

The slope is the same as Lecture 16's, -0.062. Only the meaning of the intercept
changed: occupancy in the middle year.

## Fix 2: rescaling {.smaller}

```{r}
av <- readRDS(url("https://github.com/bmaitner/biometry_course/raw/refs/heads/main/data/Avonet/AVONET1_BirdLife.rds"))
birds <- na.omit(av[, c("Migration", "Range.Size", "Mass")])
birds$migrant <- as.integer(birds$Migration == 3)

mig_nll <- function(p, range, mass){
  prob <- plogis(p[1] + p[2] * range + p[3] * mass)
  -sum(dbinom(birds$migrant, size = 1, prob = prob, log = TRUE))
}

fit_raw <- optim(c(0, 0, 0), mig_nll, range = birds$Range.Size, mass = birds$Mass)
c(fit_raw$par, nll = fit_raw$value)

fit_sc <- optim(c(0, 0, 0), mig_nll, range = birds$Range.Size / 1e6,
                mass = birds$Mass / 1000, method = "BFGS")
c(fit_sc$par, nll = fit_sc$value)
```

## What rescaling showed {.smaller}

In km² and grams, Nelder-Mead stops at more than twice the best NLL, with the
range effect negative. In millions of km² and kg, the range effect is positive:
migrants have larger ranges, which fits, since their ranges include both breeding
and wintering grounds.

. . .

A check with `glm()`, which fits logistic models directly:

```{r}
glm(migrant ~ I(Range.Size / 1e6) + I(Mass / 1000), family = binomial,
    data = birds)$coefficients
```

## Fix 3: an unprotected fit {.smaller}

```{r}
hump_nat <- function(p){
  mu <- p[1] * exp(-(reef$depth - p[2])^2 / (2 * p[3]^2))
  -sum(dnbinom(reef$richness, mu = mu, size = p[4], log = TRUE))
}

start <- c(25, 10, 20, 0.2)
fit_nat <- suppressWarnings(optim(start, hump_nat, method = "BFGS"))
c(fit_nat$par, nll = fit_nat$value)
```

A peak 328 m deep, in data that stop at 32 m. On the way, the search tried a
negative size and a negative peak.

## Fix 3: transformed, and bounded {.smaller}

```{r}
hump_log <- function(p){
  mu <- exp(p[1]) * exp(-(reef$depth - p[2])^2 / (2 * exp(p[3])^2))
  -sum(dnbinom(reef$richness, mu = mu, size = exp(p[4]), log = TRUE))
}
fit_log <- optim(c(log(25), 10, log(20), log(0.2)), hump_log, method = "BFGS")
c(peak = exp(fit_log$par[1]), depth = fit_log$par[2], width = exp(fit_log$par[3]),
  size = exp(fit_log$par[4]), nll = fit_log$value)

fit_bnd <- optim(start, hump_nat, method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = c(0.01, 0, 0.1, 0.01))
c(fit_bnd$par, nll = fit_bnd$value)
```

Both find the hump: about 25 species at 16 m, 24 m wide.

## Fix 3: penalized {.smaller}

```{r}
hump_pen <- function(p){
  if (any(p[c(1, 3, 4)] <= 0)) {
    return(1e10)
  }
  hump_nat(p)
}

fit_pen_bfgs <- optim(start, hump_pen, method = "BFGS")
fit_pen_nm   <- optim(start, hump_pen)
rbind(bfgs = c(fit_pen_bfgs$par, nll = fit_pen_bfgs$value),
      nelder_mead = c(fit_pen_nm$par, nll = fit_pen_nm$value))
```

BFGS lands where the unprotected fit did; Nelder-Mead, which never uses a slope,
gets past the penalty's cliff to the right answer.

## The loop and `tryCatch()` {.smaller}

```{r}
lin_nll <- function(p){
  prob <- p[1] + p[2] * occ$elapsed
  -sum(dbinom(occ$n_occupied, size = occ$n_routes, prob = prob, log = TRUE))
}

set.seed(20)
results <- rep(NA, 10)
for (i in 1:10) {
  start <- c(runif(1, 0.5, 1), runif(1, -0.03, 0.01))
  results[i] <- tryCatch(
    optim(start, lin_nll, method = "BFGS")$value,
    error = function(e){ NA }
  )
}
round(results, 2)
```

Without `tryCatch()`, the loop stops at the third fit.

## Fix 4: build up from the simpler model {.smaller}

```{r}
plain_nll <- function(p){
  mu <- exp(p[1] + p[2] * counts$frac_built)
  -sum(dnbinom(counts$count, mu = mu, size = exp(p[3]), log = TRUE))
}
threshold_nll <- function(p){
  mu <- exp(p[1] + p[2] * pmax(0, counts$frac_built - p[3]))
  -sum(dnbinom(counts$count, mu = mu, size = exp(p[4]), log = TRUE))
}

fit_plain <- optim(c(2, -1, 0), plain_nll)
fit_built <- optim(c(fit_plain$par[1:2], 0, fit_plain$par[3]), threshold_nll)
c(threshold = fit_built$par[3], birds_below = exp(fit_built$par[1]),
  nll = fit_built$value)
```

A threshold of about 1.4% developed, with about 12 bobwhite expected on a route
below it: there is a threshold, but it is so close to zero that there is
effectively no safe level of development.

## The challenge, solved {.smaller}

```{r}
reef$depth10 <- reef$depth / 10
reef$vis10 <- reef$visibility / 10
reef$c_year <- reef$year - mean(reef$year)

fixed_nll <- function(p){
  mu <- exp(p[1] + p[2] * reef$depth10 + p[3] * reef$depth10^2 +
            p[4] * reef$vis10 + p[5] * reef$c_year)
  -sum(dnbinom(reef$richness, mu = mu, size = exp(p[6]), log = TRUE))
}

fit_fixed <- optim(c(3, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1), fixed_nll, method = "BFGS")
c(nll = fit_fixed$value, convergence = fit_fixed$convergence)
```

Three changes: centered year, depth and visibility in tens of metres, and size on
the log scale. The first two are what matter here; the third is good practice.

## Checking it a second way {.smaller}

```{r}
check <- MASS::glm.nb(richness ~ depth + I(depth^2) + visibility + year, data = reef)
-as.numeric(logLik(check))
```

A completely different fitting routine, on the original unscaled covariates,
reaches the same NLL. Lecture 24 covers `glm.nb()` properly.
